rationale: ANNOTATION TYPE REFERENCES (owner ruling 2026-10-18: annotations are owed relationships, not payload). An annotation names a DECLARED TYPE, so it owes a `references` row under the label this lane already uses for every type mention. The pinned tree-sitter-dart grammar gives exactly ONE node type for the construct (`annotation`; there is no Java-style `marker_annotation`), but the annotation's POSITION changes with the declaration kind — a CHILD of class_definition / enum_declaration / enum_constant / formal_parameter / local_variable_declaration, a SIBLING of the declaration inside class_body and program (probed: annotation-shapes-probe.ts, clean parse, raw trees printed there). A rule written for one position misses the others, which is why this fixture pins every position Dart permits. Pre-fix the relationship channel carried 0 rows with isAnnotation. Two spelling rules are pinned as forbids: the `@` sigil and the argument list are not part of the name; and a qualified annotation publishes the LEAF (this lane strips import aliases everywhere — DT-B/DAD1/DAD2 — unlike Java, whose qualifier is a package). The top-level `const int deprecated = 1` makes the annotation-name-is-not-a-read forbid falsifiable: without the gate, the identifier inside `@deprecated` resolves against this file's top-level values and publishes a `uses` row for the annotation's own name.

expectRelationships.note: POSITIVE 1 — a CLASS annotation. The annotation is a CHILD of class_definition (probed), not a sibling, so this row is the one a sibling-only rule misses.
POSITIVE 2 — the FIRST of two annotations on one declaration. Both must publish; a rule that unshifted and overwrote would keep only one.
POSITIVE 3 — the SECOND annotation on the same declaration, with arguments. The argument list is not part of the target name.

POSITIVE 4 — QUALIFIED annotation (`@prefix.Qualified()`). The target is the LEAF the grammar's `name` field names (a `scoped_identifier`'s name child) — the alias-prefixed spelling `prefix.Qualified` is forbidden below, and the `@`/`()` are never in the target.
POSITIVE 5 — a FIELD annotation, sibling form inside class_body (`class_body (annotation) (declaration ...)` — probed).

POSITIVE 6 — a MULTI-DECLARATOR field: one annotation decorates both variables, and the symbol model makes each declarator its own property, so each declarator gets a row (same rule as the Java lane, JLS 8.3's annotation applying to both).
POSITIVE 7 — the second declarator of the same annotated field. A rule that attributed the annotation to the declaration's FIRST name only passes POSITIVE 6 and fails this row.

POSITIVE 8 — a METHOD annotation (sibling form: `class_body (annotation) (method_signature (function_signature ...))`). The carrier is the method NAME, because the annotation decorates the declaration that publishes it.
POSITIVE 9 — an annotation WITH an argument on a method; the carrier is still the method.

POSITIVE 10 — a PARAMETER annotation. The annotation is a CHILD of `formal_parameter` (probed); a parameter publishes no symbol of its own (DARTD8), so the annotation is attributed to the callable that declares it — the same attribution rule the Java lane uses for carrier positions.
POSITIVE 11 — a GETTER annotation, carrier = the getter's published property name.
POSITIVE 12 — a CONSTRUCTOR annotation. A constructor symbol is always named `constructor` (DARTD3), so its annotation edge is sourced to the same name every other constructor row uses.
POSITIVE 13 — an ENUM CONSTANT annotation: annotation is a CHILD of `enum_constant` (probed), carrier = the constant's own symbol name.
POSITIVE 14 — a TOP-LEVEL VARIABLE annotation (program-level sibling form) attributed to the declared value, not to the module.
POSITIVE 15 — a TOP-LEVEL FUNCTION annotation. The annotation is a program sibling of `function_signature` (probed).
POSITIVE 16 — a LOCAL VARIABLE annotation. A local publishes no symbol (DARTD8), so the annotation is attributed to the enclosing function — the carrier-position rule again.

INFERRED TOP-LEVEL VARIABLE — `@deprecated final inferredTop = 6;` parses the modifier keyword as its OWN sibling between the annotation and the declarator list, so a carrier walk that took the immediate next sibling found `final_builtin` and published NOTHING. The walk now steps over the grammar's `*_builtin` modifier nodes.

TYPED const TOP-LEVEL VARIABLE (`const String typedTop`): the annotation's next siblings are `const_builtin`, `type_identifier`, `static_final_declaration_list` — the modifier-skip lands on the type node, whose declarator-list step names the variable.

INFERRED CLASS FIELD (`final inferredField = 7;`): the class-body sibling form already carried the `declaration` wrapper, so this row pins that the modifier-skip did not break the wrapping form while fixing the program-level one.

ANNOTATED TYPEDEF — the annotation is a CHILD of the `type_alias` wrapper (probed), a position the child-carrier reader did not cover; the truth oracle derived the row and the corpus gate reported the analyzer as MISSING on generic_metadata_test.dart.

TYPE-QUALIFIED annotation — `@ScopedCarrier.variant()`: the qualifier is the TYPE (the member selects a named constructor), so the target is `ScopedCarrier`, not the constructor segment. The alias table is what distinguishes this from the aliased case below; both are `scoped_identifier`.
ALIAS-QUALIFIED annotation — `@core.deprecated` where `core` is an import alias: the type is the LEAF, because the qualifier is an alias no declaration carries.

forbidRelationships.note: THE SIGIL IS NOT THE NAME: `@deprecated` parses as the annotation node's TEXT; the target must be the name node's text.
THE ARGUMENT LIST IS NOT THE NAME. `@JsonKey(name: 'renamed')` must not publish a target carrying its arguments; the same rule kills any `Name(args)` spelling.
THE ALIAS-QUALIFIED SPELLING, forbidden: this lane's types are spelled alias-free (DT-B/DAD1/DAD2). The positive row pins the leaf.

ANNOTATION NAMES ARE NOT VALUE READS, and this forbid is FALSIFIABLE: the file declares `const int deprecated = 1;`, so a missing annotation-name gate would let the identifier inside `@deprecated` resolve against the file's top-level values and publish this `uses` row.
the same rule for the method annotation name — an annotation is not a read of its own type in value position.
an annotation is a TYPE MENTION, not an import: the label must be `references`.

THE LABEL IS NOT ENOUGH — every annotation row carries `isAnnotation: true`; a `references` row to an annotation's target without the flag would be indistinguishable from an ordinary type mention and is forbidden so the distinction cannot be dropped silently.
A PARAMETER NAME PUBLISHES NO SYMBOL (DARTD8), so a parameter annotation must not be sourced to the parameter's spelling — it is attributed to the callable (`method`), pinned in the positive row.
NO MODULE-SOURCED ANNOTATION ROW: the module symbol publishes only for genuinely library-level facts in this lane; a class annotation must attribute to the class, not the file.

THE CONSTRUCTOR SEGMENT IS NOT THE TYPE — the leaf-taker this fix removes published `variant`, which answers no declared type. Together with the aliased positive row this pins the alias-table rule in both directions.
THE ALIAS-QUALIFIED SPELLING, forbidden — `core` is an import alias, so the target must be the leaf.
